Barbar Shah (temple property) and is seeking a direction on the respondents to pay compensation of the land taken over by the State without following the mandate of law contained in J&K Land Acquisition Act.
2.

The petitioner submits that the Shri Bajrang Dev Baba Dharam Dass Temple is owner of landed property measuring 60 kanals and 07 marlas situated at Estate Habbakadal (Chinar Bagh, Srinagar)
in various survey numbers, which property has been taken over by the respondents for development of recreational park without payment of compensation.

entities.text: Bajrang Dev Baba Dharam Dass Temple
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: It is submitted that with a view to claiming compensation of the property forcibly taken over by the respondents, a writ petition being OWP No.221/1994 came to be filed by Baba Mahant Ram Kankar Dass, Sole Trustee of the Temple properties, which was disposed of by a Single Bench of this Court vide order dated 29.06.1998 directing the respondents- State to treat the writ petition as representation and if it is found that the land described in the writ petition has been used by the State for public purpose then requisite steps be taken to acquire the said land under the Jammu & Kashmir Land Acquisition Act and for payment of compensation to the Trust.
The grievance of the petitioner is that neither the judgment aforesaid has been complied nor compensation has been worked out and disbursed.
3. The writ petition is opposed by the respondents.

In the reply affidavit filed by the Director,
Floriculture, Kashmir, Srinagar, it is submitted that the development of Chinar Bagh into recreational park was taken up by the Floriculture Department in March 1991 after seeking approval from the Executive Committee, SCADP headed by the Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir in December, 1990.
However, due to the objections raised by Sh. Mahant Ram Kankar Dass, the work was eventually stopped and thereafter no developmental activity has been taken on the said land.
It is further submitted that the land in question is neither under the control of Floriculture Department nor the department intends to occupy the aforesaid land.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioner, who is stranger to the temple properties, has no locus standi to file this petition.
5. The status of the petitioner to succeed to the management of the temple and its properties is not recorded in the revenue record.
Detailed discussion in this regard is made in the judgment of even date passed in OWP No.25/2018.

In terms of the aforesaid judgment, the temple properties have been put under the management of a Committee to be constituted by the District Magistrate,
Srinagar.

Since the stand of the respondents is that the said property belonging to the temple has not been utilized by the Floriculture Department nor does the Floriculture Department intends to use the same, as such, the Committee to be constituted by the District Magistrate/Deputy Commissioner, Srinagar in terms of the judgment passed in OWP No.25/2018, shall take over the aforesaid property also under its management.

6. The Committee shall also verify as to whether any property belonging to the temple is still under the occupation of the Government or any of its department and if it is found that any of the government departments is in possession of the property belonging to the temple, immediate steps shall be taken to retrieve the property.
